narrative.overview:
This system is built like precision instrumentation. It exists in a high-stakes industrial environment where every performance event is recorded permanently on a blockchain — no edits, no erasure. The interface reflects that permanence: deliberate, unambiguous, and load-bearing. Every pixel earns its place. Density is a feature, not a failure.

The visual language pairs a dark charcoal navigation rail with a clean, bright content area. The sidebar is the anchor — always present, always grounding the operator or manager in where they are and what role they hold. The content area is neutral and bright, designed to make data the protagonist. Bridgestone red appears as a precise signal: active navigation state, primary action, critical status. It is never decorative.

The system explicitly rejects: the default blue-and-white admin aesthetic; consumer-app decoration; the hacker dark-mode terminal aesthetic; and joyless corporate grey that communicates indifference to the people this system evaluates.
keyCharacteristics: Dark navigation rail (#111827) paired with bright content area (#f5f7fa) — structured contrast, not uniform tone
Bridgestone red used at ≤10% of any screen surface — its scarcity makes it signal
Inter as the sole typeface across all weights — consistency communicates control
Flat-by-default cards, lifted on hover — stillness is authority; elevation is earned
Color carries meaning, never decoration — red is warning/action, green is merit, white is truth

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Red appears as a signal, not a brand wash. Reserve it for: active nav item, primary button, misconduct badges, and critical warnings. Nowhere else.

rules.name: The Anti-Cream Rule
rules.body: The content background is #f5f7fa — a cool grey-blue, not a warm off-white. This is a factory floor system, not an editorial magazine.

rules.name: The Weight-as-Voice Rule
rules.body: This system uses one font family across all contexts. Hierarchy is carried entirely by weight and size, not by font switching.

rules.name: The Extrabold Ceiling
rules.body: Font weight 800 is reserved for KPI numbers in operator info cards and display-level rank indicators only.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards do not assert elevation at rest. The ambient shadow reads as separation, not depth. Elevation is earned through interaction, not decoration.

rules.name: The Colored Shadow Principle
rules.body: When a shadow appears on a colored element, it uses a tinted version of that element's color — never a generic rgba(0,0,0,x).

rules.name: The Color-Is-Not-Enough Rule
rules.body: Activity type must be labeled in text alongside color. Never rely solely on green/red to distinguish merit from misconduct.

dos: Do use Bridgestone Red (#ef4444) on ≤10% of any screen surface. Its scarcity makes it signal.
Do keep the sidebar dark (#111827) and the content area bright (#f5f7fa). This contrast is the system's structural identity.
Do use #6b7280 or darker for placeholder text to meet WCAG 2.1 AA 4.5:1 contrast against white.
Do always pair the merit/misconduct green/red signal with a text label or icon — color alone is never sufficient.
Do use colored tinted shadows on brand-colored elements.
Do use 8px radius on interactive elements, 12px on cards, 16px on featured hero elements.
Do keep KPI metric numbers at 2rem 700 weight maximum.
Do use Inter at weights 400–700 for all body and UI. Weight 800 only for display KPI numbers.
Do cap body text at 65–75ch maximum line length.
Do include @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) for every transition and hover animation.
Do use flat semantic fills for KPI icon blocks — one color per semantic role, no multi-stop gradients.
donts: Don't use a generic blue as the primary action color. The real product primary is Bridgestone Red.
Don't use the warm cream/sand/off-white band for backgrounds. The content area is Workshop Light (#f5f7fa) — cool grey-blue.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Prohibited.
Don't use a colored border-left stripe (>1px) as the sole distinguishing treatment for cards or list items.
Don't use emoji as primary UI indicators. Replace with Ionicons and semantic color + text labels.
Don't apply multi-stop gradient fills to KPI icon blocks. Use flat semantic fills.
Don't make the app feel like a generic blue admin panel. The dark rail and red accent are the primary differentiators.
Don't use consumer-app patterns: bright bubble gradients, oversized rounded pill cards, playful illustrations.
Don't extend the dark aesthetic to the content area. Sidebar dark, content area light.
Don't produce cold, grey, and lifeless screens.
